`<#>` orders by **bounding-box** distance; nearest-per-row needs **LATERAL**. The same idea for vectors is in [Distance metrics and exact search](/e1/distance-and-exact-search).

lessons.title: Everyday spatial queries
lessons.tldr: Most map features are built from a handful of spatial operations: point-in-polygon joins, buffers, unions, clusters and GeoJSON output. Running them inside PostgreSQL keeps the data, its indexes and its validity rules in one place, so the answers stay correct and fast as the data grows.

visualizer.title: A point-in-polygon join and a DBSCAN run, step by step
visualizer.interaction: Step the join zone by zone: box candidates first, then the exact test. Switch to **ST_ClusterDBSCAN**, set eps and minpoints, and watch core, border and noise points appear.

presets.label: Orders per zone
presets.lookFor: Z25, Z15 and Z07 hold the hubs (about 1 000 orders each). The plan loops over 33 zones and probes the orders index with `Index Cond: (geom @ z.geom)`, then `Filter: st_contains`: **Rows Removed by Filter: 44** per zone on average.

presets.label: Contains vs covers
presets.lookFor: A point exactly on a zone corner: `ST_Contains` says **0** zones (a polygon does not contain its own boundary), `ST_Covers` and `ST_Intersects` say **2**. Pick the one that matches your counting rule.

presets.label: Buffer, length, area
presets.lookFor: The road is **15 097 m** long; its 300 m corridor covers 9.34 km². To count orders near it, `ST_DWithin` (index-aware) beats testing against a buffer polygon.

presets.label: ST_Union vs ST_Collect
presets.lookFor: `ST_Union` **dissolves** the shared edges: 7 hexagons (49 vertices) become one Polygon of 19 vertices and 40.92 km² (7 × 5.85). `ST_Collect` only bundles them into a 7-part collection: much cheaper, but the inner edges stay.

presets.label: Clusters: DBSCAN and k-means
presets.lookFor: DBSCAN finds the **4 hubs** (about 800 orders each), one small extra cluster, and **1 745** noise orders with a NULL id. k-means returns exactly k clusters (more only if you pass `max_radius`), so every order is forced into one of 4.

presets.label: GeoJSON for a web map
presets.lookFor: GeoJSON coordinates must be **longitude/latitude (4326)**, so transform first. Six decimals is about 0.1 m. Simplifying the outline by 500 m and trimming decimals cuts the payload from 1 285 to 752 characters.

presets.label: Validity
presets.lookFor: A "bow-tie" ring crosses itself at (1 1). Its signed areas cancel, so `ST_Area` says **0**. `ST_MakeValid` splits it into two triangles with area **2**. PostGIS does not validate on insert.

production.title: A delivery-zone dashboard
production.problem: Counts were wrong in two ways. Orders on a shared zone border were counted twice, because the query used `ST_Intersects`. A few hand-drawn zones were self-intersecting, and their `ST_Area` and contains tests silently gave nonsense.
production.outcome: Every order is counted at most once, the constraint blocks new invalid zones, and the map loads one compact JSON document. In the playground the 33-zone join runs in about 10 ms through the orders index.

pitfalls.title: Double counting on shared borders
pitfalls.fix: Use `ST_Contains` (excludes the boundary) and decide what to do with exact-boundary points, or pick one zone per point with `DISTINCT ON`.

pitfalls.title: Invalid polygons in, nonsense out
pitfalls.fix: Repair once, then enforce.

pitfalls.title: Simplify breaking shapes
pitfalls.fix: Use `ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology` for validity, or `ST_CoverageSimplify` to keep shared edges between neighbours. Simplify in a metric SRID with a tolerance in metres.

pitfalls.title: Buffering to find what is near
pitfalls.fix: Use `ST_DWithin(geom, $1, 500)`. It is exact and index-aware.

keyPointers: Point-in-polygon join: `JOIN … ON ST_Contains(zone, point)`. The index probe uses the zone box, then the exact test filters.
`ST_Contains` excludes the boundary; `ST_Covers` and `ST_Intersects` include it.
`ST_Union` dissolves into one shape; `ST_Collect` only bundles. `ST_ClusterDBSCAN` returns NULL for noise; `ST_ClusterKMeans` makes exactly k clusters unless given `max_radius`.
GeoJSON output is longitude/latitude: `ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_Transform(geom, 4326), 6)`.
Check `ST_IsValid` on load and enforce it with a constraint. Start again from [Spatial indexes](/e4/spatial-indexes) when a query is slow.
